output.brief: The Kestria buffering is almost certainly caused by the smart-TV app 5.2 release, not the new CDN. Both went live on 9 October, which is why they look alike. Session data from 12–25 October shows smart-TV 5.2 stalling 5.9% of viewing time on all three ISPs. Every other client (web, mobile, older TV app) is at 0.6–0.7% on the same Tessaline CDN and the same ISPs. Handball viewing began after the problem started and didn't change the rate. Moving back to Corvane would not fix it. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Next steps: (1) Don't send the breach notice, withhold fees or switch back. (2) Revert the TV app's adaptive-streaming settings to 5.1 in Kestria and pause the wider 5.2 rollout until fixed. Check whether other markets will see the same issue. (3) Keep the rebuffering alert on and add app version and device breakdowns, noting the dashboard rebuild is about six weeks away. (4) Hold the win-back offer. Cancellations also followed the 1 October price rise, so buffering's share is unproven. Tessaline's slightly colder cache is a minor factor at most.
